body_html:
Units for length, mass and volume

Length is how long something is: kilometres (km), metres (m) and centimetres (cm). Mass is how heavy something is: kilograms (kg) and grams (g). Volume is how much liquid there is: litres (ℓ) and millilitres (ml).

FactAbout the same as
1 km = 1000 ma 15-minute walk
1 m = 100 cma metre rule, or one big step
1 kg = 1000 ga 1 kg bag of sugar
1 ℓ = 1000 mla carton of milk

Use the small unit for small things (an eraser in cm, a pencil in g, medicine in ml) and the big unit for big things (a trip in km, a bag of rice in kg, a bucket of water in ℓ).

Read a scale or a beaker

Not every mark has a number. First find what one mark is worth: the jump between two numbers ÷ the number of spaces. Then count on from the number before.

Compound units

A measurement like 2 m 35 cm uses two units. To change it to the smaller unit, change the big unit first, then add.

Example 1

2 m 35 cm = ? cm

2 m = 200 cm. 200 cm + 35 cm = 235 cm.

Answer: 235 cm

Example 2

3 kg 40 g = ? g

3 kg = 3000 g. 3000 g + 40 g = 3040 g. Keep the zero in 3040.

Answer: 3040 g

To change back, take out the thousands (or hundreds for cm).

Example 3

1250 ml = ? ℓ ? ml

1250 ml = 1000 ml + 250 ml. 1000 ml = 1 ℓ.

Answer: 1 ℓ 250 ml

Use a bar model

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 kg 40 g = 340 g3 kg = 3000 g, so 3 kg 40 g = 3040 g
1 km = 100 m1 km = 1000 m (1 m = 100 cm)
2 m + 35 cm = 37Add metres to metres and cm to cm: 2 m 35 cm
1250 ml = 12 ℓ 50 ml1000 ml make 1 ℓ: 1250 ml = 1 ℓ 250 ml
Counting every mark as 10Find what one mark is worth: jump ÷ spaces
Forgetting to rename4 m − 35 cm: rename 4 m as 3 m 100 cm

faq.q: What is taught in P3 length, mass and volume?
faq.a: In Primary 3, students measure length in km, m and cm, mass in kg and g, and volume in ℓ and ml. They use compound units such as 2 m 35 cm and change them to the smaller unit and back.

faq.q: How do I explain 3 kg 40 g = 3040 g to my child?
faq.a: Change the kilograms first: 3 kg = 3000 g. Then add the grams: 3000 g + 40 g = 3040 g, so the zero stays in the hundreds place.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with compound units?
faq.a: The most common mistake is writing the two numbers side by side, so 3 kg 40 g becomes 340 g. Another is thinking that 1 km = 100 m; it is 1000 m.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Measuring length in km, volume in ml, and converting compound units (km and m, m and cm, kg and g, ℓ and ml) are part of Primary 3 Measurement in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus.

sets.title: Choose the unit: km, m, cm, kg, g, ℓ and ml

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of an eraser?
items.e: An eraser is short. It fits on a 30 cm ruler, so use centimetres. Kilograms measure mass.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the height of an HDB block of flats?
items.e: An HDB block is very tall, but you can see the top. Use metres. Litres measure volume.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the distance from Changi Airport to the Singapore Zoo?
items.e: That is a long trip by car or MRT, so use kilometres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a swimming pool?
items.e: You can swim from one end of a pool to the other, so use metres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a mandarin orange?
items.e: A mandarin orange is light. It fits in your hand, so use grams.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a bag of rice?
items.e: A bag of rice is heavy to carry, so use kilograms.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is very light, so use grams. Centimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the volume of medicine in a teaspoon?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, so use millilitres. Grams measure mass.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the volume of water in a bucket?
items.e: A bucket holds a lot of water, so use litres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the volume of juice in a packet drink?
items.e: A packet drink from the canteen holds a small amount, so use millilitres.

items.q: 1 km = ? m
items.e: Kilo means 1000. So 1 km = 1000 m. 1 km is not 100 m.

items.q: 1 m = ? cm
items.e: A metre rule has 100 centimetres marked on it. So 1 m = 100 cm.

items.q: 1 kg = ? g
items.e: Kilo means 1000. So 1 kg = 1000 g.

items.q: 1 ℓ = ? ml
items.e: 1000 millilitres fill 1 litre: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A ruler is about ? long.
items.e: A ruler fits in your school bag. It is about 30 cm long. 30 m is longer than a classroom.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A bottle of water holds about ?
items.e: A water bottle is small, so it holds about 500 ml. 500 ℓ would fill a big tank.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A Primary 3 pupil has a mass of about ?
items.e: Most P3 pupils have a mass between 20 kg and 35 kg. 28 g is the mass of a few coins.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. You can walk about ? in 15 minutes.
items.e: A 15-minute walk covers about 1 km. You walk 1 m in one big step.

items.q: Which is longer: 1 km or 900 m?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. 1000 m is longer than 900 m, so 1 km is longer, even though 1 looks small.

items.q: Which holds more: a 1 ℓ carton of milk or a 950 ml bottle of juice?
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml. 1000 ml is more than 950 ml, so the carton holds more. Change to the same unit before you compare.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a packet of biscuits. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 300 g: 300 g + 50 g = 350 g.
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 800 g: 800 g + 50 g = 850 g.
The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 400 g = 1 kg 400 g.
The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 7 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg + 700 g = 2 kg 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a papaya. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 6 marks past 0: 600 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of mangoes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 9 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 900 g = 1 kg 900 g.
The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 3 marks past 3 kg: 3 kg + 600 g = 3 kg 600 g.
The numbers go up by 1 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 g ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 1 mark past 4 kg: 4 kg + 200 g = 4 kg 200 g.

items.q: How much water is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 ml. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 200 ml ÷ 2 = 100 ml. The top of the water is 1 line above 200 ml: 200 ml + 100 ml = 300 ml.

items.q: How much orange juice is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 ml. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 100 ml ÷ 2 = 50 ml. The top of the orange juice is 1 line above 400 ml: 400 ml + 50 ml = 450 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 500 ml ÷ 5 = 100 ml. The top of the water is 4 lines above 500 ml: 500 ml + 400 ml = 900 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ml ÷ 5 = 200 ml. The top of the water is 2 lines above 1 ℓ: 1 ℓ + 400 ml = 1 ℓ 400 ml.

items.q: How much orange juice is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ml ÷ 5 = 200 ml. The top of the orange juice is 3 lines up from the bottom: 600 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ml ÷ 5 = 200 ml. The top of the water is 4 lines above 1 ℓ: 1 ℓ + 800 ml = 1 ℓ 800 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 ℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ml ÷ 4 = 250 ml. The top of the water is 1 line above 1 ℓ: 1 ℓ + 250 ml = 1 ℓ 250 ml.

items.q: How much orange juice is in the beaker?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 ℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ml ÷ 4 = 250 ml. The top of the orange juice is 3 lines above 2 ℓ: 2 ℓ + 750 ml = 2 ℓ 750 ml.

items.q: How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 10. 10 − 3 = 7, so it is 7 cm long.

items.q: How long is the ribbon?
items.e: From 0 to 1 m there are 10 spaces, so each mark is 100 cm ÷ 10 = 10 cm. The ribbon ends 7 marks after 1 m: 1 m + 70 cm = 1 m 70 cm.

items.q: How long is the rope?
items.e: From 0 to 1 m there are 10 spaces, so each mark is 100 cm ÷ 10 = 10 cm. The rope ends 4 marks after 2 m: 2 m + 40 cm = 2 m 40 cm.

items.q: How long is the plank?
items.e: From 0 to 1 m there are 10 spaces, so each mark is 100 cm ÷ 10 = 10 cm. The plank ends 2 marks after 3 m: 3 m + 20 cm = 3 m 20 cm.

sets.title: Change compound units to cm, m, g or ml

items.q: 3 m = ? cm
2 m 35 cm = ? cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 2 m = 200 cm. Then 200 cm + 35 cm = 235 cm.

items.q: 6 m 70 cm = ? cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 6 m = 600 cm. Then 600 cm + 70 cm = 670 cm.

items.q: 6 km = ? m
1 kg 600 g = ? g
2 kg 750 g = ? g
1 ℓ 250 ml = ? ml
3 ℓ 500 ml = ? ml
1 km 200 m = ? m
3 km 450 m = ? m
4 m 8 cm = ? cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 4 m = 400 cm. Then 400 cm + 8 cm = 408 cm. Keep the zero: 4 m 8 cm is 408 cm, not 48 cm.

items.q: 3 kg 40 g = ? g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so 3 kg = 3000 g. Then 3000 g + 40 g = 3040 g. Keep the zeros: 3 kg 40 g is 3040 g, not 340 g.

items.q: 2 ℓ 80 ml = ? ml
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 2 ℓ = 2000 ml. Then 2000 ml + 80 ml = 2080 ml. Keep the zeros: 2 ℓ 80 ml is 2080 ml, not 280 ml.

items.q: Nurul says 2 kg 60 g = 260 g. Is she right? What is 2 kg 60 g in grams?
items.e: Nurul is not right. 2 kg = 2000 g, not 200 g. 2000 g + 60 g = 2060 g.

items.q: Which is the same as 2 m 5 cm?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 cm + 5 cm = 205 cm. 250 cm is 2 m 50 cm.

items.q: 5 km 60 m = ? m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so 5 km = 5000 m. Then 5000 m + 60 m = 5060 m. Keep the zeros: 5 km 60 m is 5060 m, not 560 m.

items.q: 4 kg 5 g = ? g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so 4 kg = 4000 g. Then 4000 g + 5 g = 4005 g. Keep the zeros: 4 kg 5 g is 4005 g, not 45 g.

items.q: 2 km 5 m = ? m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so 2 km = 2000 m. Then 2000 m + 5 m = 2005 m. Keep the zeros: 2 km 5 m is 2005 m, not 25 m.

items.q: 5 ℓ 5 ml = ? ml
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 5 ℓ = 5000 ml. Then 5000 ml + 5 ml = 5005 ml. Keep the zeros: 5 ℓ 5 ml is 5005 ml, not 55 ml.

items.q: Which is heavier: 2 kg 90 g or 2900 g?
items.e: Change to grams: 2 kg 90 g = 2000 g + 90 g = 2090 g. 2900 g is more than 2090 g, so 2900 g is heavier.

sets.title: Change to compound units, add and subtract

items.q: 1250 ml = ? ℓ ? ml
305 cm = ? m ? cm
items.e: 305 cm = 300 cm + 5 cm. 300 cm = 3 m, so 305 cm = 3 m 5 cm.

items.q: 450 cm = ? m ? cm
508 cm = ? m ? cm
items.e: 508 cm = 500 cm + 8 cm. 500 cm = 5 m, so 508 cm = 5 m 8 cm.

items.q: 3009 ml = ? ℓ ? ml
Which is longer: 3 m 5 cm or 350 cm?
items.e: Change to centimetres: 3 m 5 cm = 300 cm + 5 cm = 305 cm. 350 cm is longer than 305 cm.

items.q: Which is the most?
items.e: Change all to ml: 2 ℓ 50 ml = 2050 ml, 2 ℓ 5 ml = 2005 ml, 2 ℓ 250 ml = 2250 ml. 2500 ml is the most.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change all to m: 4 km 80 m = 4080 m, 4800 m, 4 km 200 m = 4200 m, 4 km 8 m = 4008 m. 4008 m is the shortest.

items.q: 2 m 45 cm + 1 m 30 cm = ?
items.e: Add the metres: 2 m + 1 m = 3 m. Add the centimetres: 45 cm + 30 cm = 75 cm. So the answer is 3 m 75 cm. Do not add 2 + 45 + 1 + 30 as one number.
Rename 4 m as 3 m 100 cm. 100 cm − 35 cm = 65 cm. So the answer is 3 m 65 cm.
800 g + 400 g = 1200 g = 1 kg 200 g. 2 kg + 1 kg + 1 kg 200 g = 4 kg 200 g. Do not forget the 1 kg from renaming.
Rename 5 ℓ as 4 ℓ 1000 ml. 1000 ml − 300 ml = 700 ml and 4 ℓ − 1 ℓ = 3 ℓ. So the answer is 3 ℓ 700 ml.
200 m is less than 500 m, so rename 1 km: 3 km 200 m = 2 km 1200 m. 1200 m − 500 m = 700 m and 2 km − 1 km = 1 km. So the answer is 1 km 700 m.

items.q: Kumar has a ribbon 2 m 40 cm long. He cuts off 85 cm to wrap a present. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 2 m 40 cm = 240 cm. Cutting off takes away: 240 cm − 85 cm = 155 cm = 1 m 55 cm.

items.q: Arjun walks 1 km 300 m to the MRT station. Then he walks 450 m to the library. How far does he walk in all?
items.e: Add the metres: 300 m + 450 m = 750 m. So he walks 1 km 750 m. 1 km is 1000 m, not 100 m.

items.q: Mrs Lim has 3 kg 200 g of rice. She cooks 1 kg 500 g of it. How much rice is left?
items.e: 3 kg 200 g = 2 kg 1200 g. 1200 g − 500 g = 700 g and 2 kg − 1 kg = 1 kg. 1 kg 700 g of rice is left.

items.q: A durian has a mass of 1 kg 800 g. A pineapple has a mass of 1 kg 350 g. How much heavier is the durian?
items.e: Both have 1 kg, so compare the grams: 800 g − 350 g = 450 g. The durian is 450 g heavier.

items.q: A jug has 2 ℓ of water. Ahmad pours 3 cups of 250 ml from it. How much water is left in the jug?
Wei Ming cuts a rope 3 m 60 cm long into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 m 60 cm = 360 cm. 4 units = 360 cm, so 1 unit = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 cm. Do not divide only the 60 cm.

items.q: Ethan buys 5 packets of soya bean milk. Each packet holds 250 ml. How much soya bean milk is there in all?
Siti’s bus ride to school is 4 km 600 m. Her friend’s MRT ride is 2 km 800 m. How much longer is the bus ride?
items.e: 4 km 600 m = 3 km 1600 m. 1600 m − 800 m = 800 m and 3 km − 2 km = 1 km. The bus ride is 1 km 800 m longer.

items.q: Mr Tan’s pail can hold 8 ℓ of water. It has 5 ℓ 750 ml of water now. How much more water is needed to fill it?
items.e: 8 ℓ = 7 ℓ 1000 ml. 1000 ml − 750 ml = 250 ml and 7 ℓ − 5 ℓ = 2 ℓ. 2 ℓ 250 ml more is needed.

items.q: Ryan’s school bag has a mass of 3 kg 400 g. He takes out a book of 650 g. What is the mass of the bag now?
items.e: 3 kg 400 g = 2 kg 1400 g. 1400 g − 650 g = 750 g. The bag is now 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: On Sports Day, 4 pupils run a relay. Each pupil runs 400 m. How far do they run in all?
A chicken rice stall uses 2 kg 500 g of rice each day. How much rice does it use in 3 days?
items.e: 3 × 2500 g = 7500 g = 7 kg 500 g. Remember that 3 × 500 g = 1500 g = 1 kg 500 g.

items.q: Zhi Hao is 1 m 32 cm tall. Ali is 1 m 28 cm tall. How much taller is Zhi Hao?
items.e: Both are 1 m and more, so compare the centimetres: 32 cm − 28 cm = 4 cm.

items.q: Mdm Wong has 2 kg of flour. She uses 750 g to make kueh and 500 g to make bread. How much flour is left?
items.e: She uses 750 g + 500 g = 1250 g. 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 g − 1250 g = 750 g of flour is left.

items.q: Chloe travels 6 km 200 m from home to Gardens by the Bay. Then she travels home the same way. How far does she travel in all?
items.e: Two equal trips: 6 km 200 m + 6 km 200 m = 12 km 400 m.

items.q: A bottle has 2 ℓ 400 ml of juice. The juice is shared equally among 4 children. How much juice does each child get?
items.e: 2 ℓ 400 ml = 2400 ml. 4 units = 2400 ml, so 1 unit = 2400 ÷ 4 = 600 ml.

items.q: A box of mandarin oranges for Chinese New Year has a mass of 4 kg 250 g. The empty box has a mass of 750 g. What is the mass of the oranges?
items.e: 4 kg 250 g = 3 kg 1250 g. 1250 g − 750 g = 500 g. The oranges have a mass of 3 kg 500 g.

items.q: Hui Min cycles 2 km 750 m at East Coast Park in the morning and 1 km 500 m in the evening. How far does she cycle in all?
How many 250 ml cups can be filled from 2 ℓ of water?
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2000 ml. 4 cups of 250 ml make 1000 ml, so 2000 ml fills 2 × 4 = 8 cups.

items.q: Devi is 1 m 25 cm tall. Her father is 50 cm taller than her. Her brother is 30 cm shorter than her father. How tall is her brother?
items.e: Father: 1 m 25 cm + 50 cm = 1 m 75 cm. Brother: 1 m 75 cm − 30 cm = 1 m 45 cm.
